questions.q: In which month and year was the Quit India Movement formally launched by the All-India Congress Committee?
questions.a: The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 at the AICC session in Bombay (now Mumbai). A wrong answer (e.g., 1940 or 1943) reveals confusion with the Individual Satyagraha (1940–41) or the post-war INA trials, indicating the student cannot anchor the movement in its precise wartime context.

questions.q: Why did Gandhi give the “Do or Die” call in August 1942 instead of continuing negotiations?
questions.a: The Cripps Mission (March 1942) offered only post-war dominion status with a province opt-out clause, which Congress rejected as a “post-dated cheque on a crashing bank.” With the Japanese advancing to India’s borders and the British refusing immediate transfer of power, Gandhi concluded that only a mass upsurge could force a withdrawal. A wrong answer that cites only “British refusal to grant independence” misses the specific trigger (Cripps failure) and the strategic calculation that the war crisis created a unique leverage point.

questions.q: A student claims: “The Quit India Movement was entirely non-violent because Gandhi led it.” Using evidence from the underground phase, explain why this claim is inaccurate.
questions.a: After the top leadership’s arrest on 9 August, the movement saw widespread violence: cutting telegraph wires, derailing trains, burning police stations, and attacking government buildings. Socialist leaders like Jayaprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, and Aruna Asaf Ali organized underground networks that explicitly adopted sabotage. Parallel governments in Satara and Tamluk administered justice and collected revenue, functioning as de facto states. A student who insists on “entirely non-violent” confuses Gandhi’s intent with the movement’s actual trajectory once decentralized leadership took over.

questions.q: Compare the British repression during Quit India (1942–43) with that during the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930–34). Identify two escalations in severity and explain why the colonial state escalated.
questions.a: Escalation 1: Use of military force including aerial strafing and machine-gunning of crowds (e.g., in Medinipur and Satara), which was absent in 1930–34. Escalation 2: Imposition of collective fines on entire villages and wholesale destruction of property, treating the movement as an internal security threat rather than a law-and-order issue. The state escalated because the movement coincided with World War II and the Japanese threat; the Viceroy Linlithgow viewed it as “the most serious rebellion since 1857” and feared it would cripple the war effort.

questions.q: Evaluate the argument: “The Quit India Movement failed because it was suppressed within a year and did not achieve immediate independence.”
questions.a: The argument is partially true but historically incomplete. While the movement was crushed by late 1943 and did not force an immediate British withdrawal, it succeeded in: (a) demonstrating that British rule lacked popular consent even during a global war, (b) making post-war independence inevitable (acknowledged by Churchill’s own War Cabinet), and (c) radicalizing a generation of youth who later filled the political vacuum. A student who judges “failure” only by short-term tactical outcome misses the strategic shift in the legitimacy of colonial rule.

questions.q: Construct a timeline with annotations showing how the Quit India Movement transformed the political landscape among the Congress, Muslim League, and the British between August 1942 and June 1945.
questions.a: A strong answer will include: Aug 1942 – Congress leaders arrested; League operates legally, expands in Punjab/Sind; 1943 – Parallel governments function till suppressed; 1944 – Gandhi released, begins talks with Jinnah (Sept); 1945 – Labour government elected in UK, Wavell Plan, Simla Conference. Annotations should link each event to the shifting triangle: Congress weakened by imprisonment, League strengthened by collaboration, British compelled to plan exit. A weak answer lists dates without analyzing the triangular power shift.
